answers.text: Tell the assistant to give three lines back every time - drop-off time, pallet count, and any damage noted.
Ask it to list every call needing follow-up as its own line - time, customer, topic, outcome - and count how many rows are on that list to get the total needing follow-up.
Something's off with the finish time in this note - starting at 8am for six hours doesn't land on the 23rd.
96 to 118 invoices is more like a 23% rise, not the 20% the note says.
Output 2, it has the actual ticket numbers behind the 88%.
Email 2, since it has the actual order volumes in it.
1. No. 2. Yes. 3. No, that's not out yet. 4. No, better not risk it. 5. No, that's personal.
I'd hold back the hourly rates and retainer cap and not paste those in.
I'd want to cross-check the reconciled totals against the warehouse count before it's finalised.

Step 4, submitting the note automatically, is the one that needs a check most since after that it's already gone through. Step 1, reading the invoice PDF, matters too because a bad read carries into everything after it.
